message.content:
I don’t have access to live data feeds, so I can’t give you the current AQI (Air Quality Index) for Los Angeles right now. However, here’s what you can do to find up‑to‑date information:

| Source | How to Use |
|--------|------------|
| **AirNow** (U.S. EPA) | Visit <https://www.airnow.gov/> and enter “Los Angeles” or your ZIP code. It shows the latest AQI, pollutant levels, and health advisories. |
| **EPA Air Quality Dashboard** | <https://www.epa.gov/air-quality-data> – provides real‑time monitoring station data. |
| **Local news sites** (e.g., LA Times, CBS Los Angeles) | Often publish daily air‑quality summaries. |
| **Weather apps** (AccuWeather, Weather.com, NOAA Weather Radar) | Many include an AQI widget. |
| **Mobile apps** (AirVisual, Plume Labs: Air Report) | Offer real‑time maps and alerts. |

If you’re looking for a quick snapshot, you can also use a search engine query like “Los Angeles air quality today” and it will pull the latest AQI from one of those sources.

Let me know if you’d like a deeper dive into how AQI is calculated or what the numbers mean!
